  - text: CLASS 9 · EUCLIDEAN GEOMETRY
  - heading "Exterior Angle Theorem" [level=1]
  - paragraph: "Objective: Relate a triangle's exterior angle to its two remote interior angles."
  - text: ◷ 10–12 min Estimated time ♙ Class 9 Grade ⌂ Geometry Subject

  - main:
    - complementary:
      - heading "Interactive Triangle Explorer" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Extend AB and drag point D to form the exterior angle ∠CBD.
      - heading "1 Extend side" [level=3]
      - paragraph: Drag point B to extend side AB.
      - text: Extended
      - checkbox "Extended" [checked]
      - heading "2 Drag exterior ray" [level=3]
      - paragraph: Drag point D to change the exterior angle.
      - slider "Exterior ray tilt": "0"
      - heading "Live Angle Measures" [level=3]
      - paragraph: ∠A (remote) 42°
      - paragraph: ∠C (remote) 73°
      - paragraph: ∠CBD (exterior) 115°
      - paragraph: ∠ABC (adjacent) 65°
      - img
      - text: Excellent!
      - strong: ∠CBD = ∠A + ∠C
      - text: 115° = 42° + 73°
      - paragraph: The Exterior Angle Theorem holds.
    - article:
      - button "Reset Diagram":
        - img
        - text: Reset Diagram
      - img "Interactive exterior angle triangle": A C B D 42° 73° 65° 115°
      - paragraph: ∠A and ∠C are the remote interior angles.
      - paragraph: ∠CBD is the exterior angle at B.
      - heading "Equation Balance" [level=3]
      - paragraph: ∠CBD = ∠A + ∠C
      - text: 115° = 42° + 73°
    - article:
      - heading "💡 Why it works" [level=2]
      - paragraph: The exterior angle and the adjacent interior angle form a linear pair (sum 180°). The three interior angles of a triangle sum to 180°.
      - paragraph: So,
      - strong: ∠CBD + ∠ABC = 180°
      - strong: (∠A + ∠B + ∠C) − ∠ABC = 180°
      - text: ∴ ∠CBD = ∠A + ∠C
    - article:
      - heading "🚀 Worked Example" [level=2]
      - paragraph: If the remote interior angles are 42° and 73°, find the exterior angle.
      - img: 42° 73° 115°
      - paragraph: x = 42° + 73° = 115°
      - text: Exterior angle = 115°
    - article:
      - heading "⊗ Common Misconception" [level=2]
      - paragraph: The adjacent interior angle is NOT one of the two remote interior angles.
      - img: × 42° 73° 115°
      - text: "Incorrect: ∠CBD ≠ ∠A + ∠ABC (115° ≠ 42° + 65°)"
    - 'heading "🏆 Your Turn: Challenge" [level=2]'
    - paragraph: The exterior angle at B is 128°. One remote interior angle (at A) is 55°. What is the measure of the other remote interior angle (at C)?
    - img: 55° x° 128°
    - heading "Find ∠C" [level=3]
    - text: x =
    - spinbutton "Challenge remote angle": "73"
    - text: °

    - complementary:

      - heading "Correct!" [level=2]
      - strong: ∠C = 73°
      - paragraph: "Check: 55° + 73° = 128°"
    - heading "☆ Key Takeaway" [level=2]
    - paragraph: An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.
    - strong: ∠CBD = ∠A + ∠C
